meta.blurb: Ada, a retired ferry captain, writes four rules on four white cards for her neighbour Leo. He runs a bicycle shop and says yes too quickly. The first rule is to mean what you say. The other three are just as simple.
meta.bible: Leo: a young man who runs a small bicycle shop on Harbour Road; kind, hurried, and in the habit of saying yes too quickly. Ada: his older neighbour, a retired captain of the ferry called the Gull; calm, dry-humoured and patient. Mira: Leo's assistant, who works three afternoons a week. Kemal: a customer whose bicycle is late. Tess: a young apprentice who joins at the end. The four rules on four white cards: Rule one, mean what you say. Rule two, take one breath before you answer. Rule three, ask before you decide what is true. Rule four, leave every place and person a little better than you found them. Days named: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. Slow breathing: in for four, out for six. Voice: warm, practical, gently humorous, never preachy; each beat teaches one clear idea. No invented studies or numbers. The rules are habits, not a test. Harbour Road: the street of the shop, with the bakery, a hardware shop and a cafe. The bay: the grey water the Gull crossed for forty years. Nell: the baker next door, who has a flour-dusted delivery bicycle. Bram: owns the hardware shop on Harbour Road. Joss: Leo's old friend, who moves flat. Pavel: the parts driver who delivers wheels and frames. Ines: Leo's sister. Dilys: an elderly customer with a squeaky bicycle bell. Hale: a customer who is angry about a bill. Sam: a customer whose daughter wants wheels for her birthday. Mira is Leo's assistant; Tess joins in the last chapter. The story runs from one October to the next. Gus: owns the cafe on the corner of Harbour Road, which closed twice one month. The Gull still crosses the bay, and its horn sounds over the water. Leo keeps a small blue notebook headed Promises, with pages for Breaths and Questions. Ada keeps the cards under a smooth grey stone with a white stripe; the fourth card has the small words and every person. Leo's puncture clinic runs on the first Saturday of each month, two hours, free. Tess is seventeen. Hale's review changes from one star to four. Season order: October, winter, spring (April delivery), summer, then October a year later.

beats.scene: Leo stands among half-mended bicycles in his cluttered shop at closing time
beats.summary: Leo, who runs a small bicycle shop, ends a hard week feeling that life has become too tangled.

beats.scene: Kemal wheels a bicycle with a badly bent front wheel through the shop door
beats.summary: On Monday Kemal brings in a bent wheel, and Leo promises it will be ready on Friday without checking.

beats.scene: Nell the baker leans on the counter beside a flour-dusted delivery bicycle
beats.summary: On Tuesday Nell the baker asks for her delivery bicycle by Wednesday morning, and Leo says yes.

beats.scene: Mira points at a crowded weekly chart pinned above the workbench
beats.summary: Mira, his assistant, shows Leo that he has promised three different jobs for the same Wednesday afternoon.

beats.scene: Leo holds the shop telephone to his ear while Mira raises her eyebrows
beats.summary: That evening a friend called Joss asks for help moving house on Saturday, and Leo agrees without thinking.

beats.scene: Leo watches Harbour Road from the shop window for a van that never comes
beats.summary: The wheel part for Kemal's bicycle does not arrive, because Leo never confirmed the order with Pavel, the parts driver.

beats.scene: Leo eats a dry biscuit standing up while two telephones ring at once
beats.summary: On Friday every yes Leo has given comes due at once, and he has no time even for lunch.

beats.scene: Kemal checks his watch beside the unfinished bicycle with its wheel still off
beats.summary: Kemal arrives at six and finds his bicycle untouched, and he leaves disappointed and almost silent.

beats.scene: Leo sits on an upturned crate in the dim and silent shop
beats.summary: Alone after closing, Leo counts the people he has let down this week and feels tired and ashamed.

beats.scene: A lit kitchen window glows beyond a low garden wall at dusk
beats.summary: Out in his back yard, Leo sees the light in his neighbour Ada's kitchen and hears her humming.

beats.scene: Ada in a woollen hat holds a steaming mug out over the garden wall
beats.summary: Ada, a retired ferry captain, sees Leo's face and offers him a mug of tea over the garden wall.

beats.scene: Leo and Ada lean on either side of the wall holding mugs
beats.summary: Leo pours out the whole story of his week, and Ada listens without interrupting.

beats.scene: A framed photograph shows a small white ferry crossing grey water
beats.summary: Ada tells Leo that she was captain of the ferry called the Gull on the bay for forty years.

beats.scene: A small ferry rocks among dark waves under a stormy sky
beats.summary: In a storm, Ada says, nobody can steer a ferry with a hundred clever ideas; she used a few clear rules.

beats.scene: A pencil-ticked paper checklist is pinned beside a kitchen window
beats.summary: Ada shows Leo the checklist pinned beside her kitchen window and says that pilots and sailors use them.

beats.scene: A pencil rests on a checklist beside a mug of tea on a table
beats.summary: A tired mind forgets even what it knows well, Ada explains, so a list does the remembering.

beats.scene: Ada and Leo sit at a wooden kitchen table with two cups between them
beats.summary: Ada tells Leo that he is not careless; he simply has no rules for the moments when he is tired.

beats.scene: Ada opens a kitchen drawer and lifts out four plain white cards
beats.summary: Ada fetches four white cards and a pen and says she will write four rules, and only four.

beats.scene: Ada writes slowly in upright letters, pausing between each word
beats.summary: Ada writes each rule slowly, weighing every word as if she were plotting a course.

beats.scene: Four white cards lie fanned out on the table beside a teapot
beats.summary: Ada reads the four rules aloud, and says she will give Leo the cards one at a time, as habits.

beats.scene: Kemal waits at the shop door on Saturday, helmet under his arm
beats.summary: On Saturday morning Kemal comes back, and Leo apologises plainly and takes the blame.

beats.scene: A bus timetable and a market street at sunrise, with one lonely walker
beats.summary: Kemal explains that he starts at five at the fish market, when no bus runs, and the bicycle was his only way there.

beats.scene: Leo fits a new wheel into Kemal's bicycle at the cluttered workbench
beats.summary: The right wheel finally arrives and the repair takes only forty minutes: the promise, not the job, was the problem.

beats.scene: Kemal wheels the mended bicycle to the shop door and gives a small nod
beats.summary: Kemal says that next time he would rather hear the true day than a pleasant one.

beats.scene: Nell pushes a pram full of fresh loaves along Harbour Road
beats.summary: Nell collects her delivery bicycle three days late and says, dryly, that she delivered bread from a pram.

beats.scene: Leo arrives at a doorway stacked with boxes and finds nobody needs him
beats.summary: Leo reaches Joss's new flat too late to help, and a second yes is broken in one day.

beats.scene: Leo walks along the harbour wall at dusk with his hands in his pockets
beats.summary: Walking home, Leo adds up the week: three people let down, himself exhausted, and nothing gained.

beats.scene: Leo knocks at Ada's front door holding a paper bag of warm buns
beats.summary: On Sunday morning Leo brings buns from Nell's bakery to Ada's door, ready to hear the first rule.

beats.scene: Ada pours tea at her kitchen table, chin resting on her hand
beats.summary: Ada hears the story of Saturday and says Leo has already done the hardest part: noticing what his words have cost.

beats.scene: Ada lays a white card on the table between buns and teapot
beats.summary: Ada lays down the first card, mean what you say, and Leo cannot stop looking at it.

beats.scene: Ada taps the white card and raises one finger beside her teacup
beats.summary: Ada explains that many ordinary sentences are small promises, and asks Leo only to count his for one day.

beats.scene: Leo counts on his fingers behind the counter: call, email, visit, coffee
beats.summary: On Monday Leo counts his promises on his fingers, and by lunchtime there are seven.

beats.scene: A notepad lists the phrases: I'll call you, leave it with me, no problem
beats.summary: Leo notices which everyday phrases hide promises: leave it with me, I'll look into it, no problem.

beats.scene: Mira sits on a wobbly stool and laughs at Leo across the shop
beats.summary: Mira reminds Leo that in July he promised her a new stool, and she is still sitting on the wobbly one.

beats.scene: Leo crosses out items on a crowded list, leaving only a few
beats.summary: Leo writes out every promise still waiting to be kept and marks the ones he cannot keep, ready to tell the truth about them.

beats.scene: Ada places a short list beside a very long list on her kitchen table
beats.summary: Ada says that the answer is to promise less, not to speak less, and to give a date only after looking at the work.

beats.scene: A customer nods at the counter as Leo writes a time in his book
beats.summary: Leo tries a new answer: instead of yes, no problem, he says he will check and telephone by four o'clock.

beats.scene: Leo counts spare inner tubes on a stockroom shelf with a pencil in hand
beats.summary: Leo counts his spare tubes and reads his work list before giving any date, and the honest answer is Wednesday.

beats.scene: Leo dials the telephone on the counter while the shop clock shows four
beats.summary: At four o'clock exactly Leo telephones the customer with his honest answer, and she is astonished and pleased.

beats.scene: Leo and Ada talk over the garden wall as a lamp comes on
beats.summary: Leo tells Ada that keeping a small promise felt surprisingly good, and she says that this is how trust begins.

beats.scene: Nell stands at the counter with her bicycle chain hanging loose
beats.summary: Nell asks Leo to mend her snapped chain by six tomorrow morning, and he feels the old yes rising.

beats.scene: Leo shakes his head kindly and points to the clock on the wall
beats.summary: Leo tells Nell honestly that six is impossible but noon is certain, and he offers to bring the bicycle himself.

beats.scene: Leo smiles and shakes his head politely at Bram outside the shop
beats.summary: Bram asks for three bicycles to be serviced by tomorrow, and Leo offers one now and two next week.

beats.scene: Ada counts three things on her fingers while Leo takes notes
beats.summary: Ada says that a kind no has three parts: thank them, be clear, and offer what you honestly can.

beats.scene: Leo phones beside a stack of tyres while a pump rests on the counter
beats.summary: His sister Ines asks him to mind her market stall on Sunday, and Leo says no kindly and offers other help.

beats.scene: Mira pulls on her coat at the shop door while Leo nods
beats.summary: Mira asks to leave an hour early, and Leo can see that he has time, so his yes is a real one.

beats.scene: Leo stands in the shop doorway as neighbours wave while passing
beats.summary: Leo realises that his fear of saying no was bigger than anything that happened: nobody has disliked him.

beats.scene: Leo holds up a thin, worn brake pad and shakes his head
beats.summary: A customer asks Leo to skip a worn brake repair to save money, and he refuses because it would not be safe.

beats.scene: A woman smiles at the shop counter beside her mended bicycle
beats.summary: The customer returns and says the new brakes feel like a different bicycle, and she thanks Leo for refusing.

beats.scene: Leo and Ada sit by the garden wall as the evening settles
beats.summary: Evenings are quieter now, because fewer promises mean fewer worries, and Ada says the first card pays back its owner.

beats.scene: Leo looks at his tired reflection in the shop window and sighs
beats.summary: After a small mistake, Leo mutters to his reflection that he is useless, and Ada hears him.

beats.scene: Ada stands in the shop doorway with a basket of vegetables
beats.summary: Ada asks whether Leo would ever speak that way to a friend, and he has to admit he would not.

beats.scene: A tally of pencil marks grows on a scrap of paper by the till
beats.summary: Leo spends a day noticing how often he says harsh things to himself, and he is shocked.

beats.scene: Ada writes two sentences side by side on a scrap of card
beats.summary: Ada shows the difference between I made a mistake, which is true, and I am a mistake, which is not.

beats.scene: Leo frowns at a slightly wobbling wheel spinning in the truing stand
beats.summary: When a wheel goes wrong, Leo says he will do it again instead of calling himself careless, and the second try is easier.

beats.scene: Two shop owners whisper by a fence while Leo walks past
beats.summary: Bram and Nell whisper about Gus, whose cafe keeps closing, and Leo feels the pull to join in.

beats.scene: Leo shrugs and steps away from two whispering neighbours at a fence
beats.summary: Leo says that he does not know and that Bram could ask Gus himself, and he goes back to work.

beats.scene: A young deckhand coils a thick rope while passengers glance at him
beats.summary: Ada tells how a false rumour about a young deckhand once ran along the quay and took a year to fade.

beats.scene: Leo points at a straight wheel and nods towards the back room
beats.summary: Leo tells Bram that Mira built the straight wheel and is the best wheel builder he has met, while she cannot hear.

beats.scene: Mira blushes at the workbench as Leo smiles at her
beats.summary: Leo tells Mira to her face that her wheels are the best he has seen, and she blushes and stands taller.

beats.scene: Leo writes the word Promises at the top of a new blue notebook
beats.summary: Leo buys a small notebook and decides to write down every promise as soon as he makes it.

beats.scene: Leo ticks his notebook beside a freshly repaired bicycle on the pavement
beats.summary: Leo ticks off his first kept promise and enjoys, for the first time, the small pleasure of a finished thing.

beats.scene: A notebook page shows six lines of promises, each with a neat tick
beats.summary: After a week there are six promises and six ticks in the notebook, and Leo feels lighter than he has in years.

beats.scene: Storm clouds gather over the coast road beyond a girl's small bicycle
beats.summary: Leo has promised Sam new wheels for his daughter's birthday on Saturday, but a storm blocks the road.

beats.scene: Leo lifts the telephone while rain rattles the shop window
beats.summary: Leo decides to tell Sam on Thursday morning, not on Saturday, because a promise that must be broken should be reported early.

beats.scene: Leo speaks on the telephone while a small loan bicycle waits beside him
beats.summary: Leo tells Sam plainly that the wheels will be late, says that he is sorry, and offers a loan bicycle for the birthday.

beats.scene: Sam smiles on the telephone beside a calendar with Saturday circled
beats.summary: Sam is disappointed but thanks Leo, because early news gives him time to plan something else.

beats.scene: A girl rides a bright loan bicycle with a ribbon on the handlebar
beats.summary: The girl rides the loan bicycle on her birthday, and on Monday Leo delivers her new wheels himself.

beats.scene: Kemal leans on the counter, reading the notebook with a raised eyebrow
beats.summary: Kemal says he heard how Leo called Sam early, and that in a small town a kept word travels fast.

beats.scene: Ada places the first white card face up in the middle of her table
beats.summary: Ada puts the first card face up in the middle of her table and says that rule one builds trust one kept promise at a time.

beats.scene: A red-faced customer waves a bill across the shop counter at Leo
beats.summary: A customer called Hale storms in on Monday, waving a bill and shouting that the price is robbery.

beats.scene: Leo leans over the counter, jaw clenched, pointing at the door
beats.summary: Stung, Leo snaps that Hale can take his business somewhere else, and Hale storms out.

beats.scene: The shop bell still swings as Leo trembles and Mira watches silently
beats.summary: Leo stands shaking after Hale leaves, and Mira says nothing, though her silence says plenty.

beats.scene: Leo studies an old ledger and a bill showing a sharp price rise
beats.summary: Leo finds that Hale has been a loyal customer for years, and that the part really did cost much more this time.

beats.scene: Ada draws a rising and falling wave on a paper napkin
beats.summary: Ada draws a wave and explains that anger rises quickly and then often fades, if we let it.

beats.scene: A ship's wheel turns gently in a captain's hands in rough water
beats.summary: Ada says that in rough water a captain turns the wheel gently, and that a person who is angry should do the same.

beats.scene: A pencil taps the napkin just below the top of the drawn wave
beats.summary: Ada says that even one slow breath lets the top of the wave begin to fall, and that is all the pause Leo needs.

beats.scene: Leo stares at the shop door where Hale left and bites his lip
beats.summary: Leo asks what to do about Hale, and Ada says to learn the pause first and mend the damage after.

beats.scene: Ada holds up a second white card in the lamplight
beats.summary: Ada gives Leo the second card: take one breath before you answer.

beats.scene: Leo turns the second card over in his fingers, doubtful and curious
beats.summary: Leo asks whether one breath can really be enough, and Ada says that one is enough to begin.

beats.scene: Leo breathes slowly with one hand on his chest in the quiet shop
beats.summary: Leo practises slow breathing in the empty shop: in for four, out for six.

beats.scene: Ada traces a long curve in the air as she breathes out slowly
beats.summary: Ada explains that a long, slow breath out helps the body to calm down, though it is not magic.

beats.scene: A customer frowns at a price tag while Leo takes a quiet breath
beats.summary: A customer asks the same question for the fifth time, and Leo takes his first working breath and answers kindly.

beats.scene: Mira tilts her head, watching Leo breathe slowly behind the counter
beats.summary: Mira notices Leo breathing and asks if he is all right; he explains, and she says she does the same before exams.

beats.scene: Leo stands at a fork in a park path, deciding which way to go
beats.summary: On a Sunday walk Leo comes to a fork in the park path and sees that a pause turns a reaction into a choice.

beats.scene: Leo sits on a bus watching a tired stranger rub his eyes
beats.summary: On a bus Leo watches a tired stranger and sees that sharp words often come from the speaker's own worries.

beats.scene: A customer stamps rain from her boots and glares at the sky
beats.summary: A customer snaps at Leo about the weather and the prices; he breathes and sees that it is not about him.

beats.scene: Ada raises one finger beside a half-open kitchen door
beats.summary: Ada warns that the pause is one breath and not a sulk, and that afterwards Leo must still answer honestly.

beats.scene: Leo holds the telephone, one hand on his chest, listening patiently
beats.summary: When his sister Ines telephones, still hurt, Leo breathes first and then listens instead of defending himself.

beats.scene: Leo writes a tally of breaths in his notebook beneath a small lamp
beats.summary: Leo starts a second page in his notebook and counts eleven breaths taken before he spoke.

beats.scene: A phone screen shows one star and a short angry message
beats.summary: A one-star online review appears, calling the shop overpriced and the owner rude.

beats.scene: Leo types quickly on his phone, his face tight and red
beats.summary: Leo's face burns, and he types three furious sentences in reply, his thumb hovering over the send button.

beats.scene: Leo lays his phone face down on the counter and breathes slowly
beats.summary: Leo remembers the second card, takes one slow breath, deletes the reply and puts the phone face down.

beats.scene: Leo reads the review again by morning light at the counter
beats.summary: The next morning Leo rereads the review calmly, sees that Hale wrote it, and admits that part of it is fair.

beats.scene: Leo writes a calm reply on his phone with a cup of tea nearby
beats.summary: Leo writes a calm reply that thanks Hale, admits he was rude, explains the price rise and offers a free check.

beats.scene: Mira reads the reply on Leo's phone with wide eyes
beats.summary: Mira reads the reply and admits that a month ago she would have expected a very different answer from Leo.

beats.scene: Hale stands stiffly in the shop doorway, holding his bicycle
beats.summary: Three days later Hale appears in the doorway with his bicycle, stiff and uncomfortable.

beats.scene: Leo and Hale talk calmly across the counter with a bicycle between them
beats.summary: Leo explains the price rise calmly, and Hale listens; neither raises his voice.

beats.scene: Leo and Hale shake hands across the counter and nod
beats.summary: Hale admits that he was angry at the bill and not at Leo, Leo says he was angry too, and they shake hands.

beats.scene: A phone screen shows four stars and a short kind message
beats.summary: That evening Hale changes his review to four stars, saying that the owner listens and puts things right.

beats.scene: Leo opens a long crate and finds the wrong bicycle frames inside
beats.summary: A crate of frames arrives in the wrong size, and one breath is not enough to cool Leo's anger.

beats.scene: Leo leaves the shop in his apron while Mira nods behind him
beats.summary: Leo remembers Ada's advice, tells Mira he needs ten minutes, and leaves before he says something he will regret.

beats.scene: Leo walks along the harbour wall with a water bottle, shoulders relaxing
beats.summary: Leo walks along the harbour wall, sips cold water, and feels the heat slowly leave his shoulders.

beats.scene: The ferry Gull crosses the bay, its horn sounding across the water
beats.summary: The horn of the Gull sounds across the bay, and Leo smiles, thinking of Ada at the wheel on far worse days.

beats.scene: Leo telephones at the counter with the wrong frames stacked beside him
beats.summary: Back in the shop, Leo telephones the supplier calmly, and with Pavel he finds that the mistake began in the warehouse.

beats.scene: Pavel hands over a crate of correct frames and shakes Leo's hand
beats.summary: The next day Pavel brings the right frames and says he is glad that Leo did not shout.

beats.scene: Leo sorts comment cards into two piles on his desk by lamplight
beats.summary: Leo opens the comment box by the door for the first time in years and sorts the cards into useful and noise.

beats.scene: A small cushioned bench stands by the shop window with a mug on it
beats.summary: The useful pile asks for a seat for waiting customers and earlier opening on Saturdays, so Leo buys a bench.

beats.scene: Ada holds a comment card up to the light and smiles
beats.summary: Ada gives Leo a question to ask of any criticism: is any of it true, and is any of it useful?

beats.scene: Ada places the second card on top of the first on her table
beats.summary: Ada lays the second card on the first and says that in the gap between feeling and speaking, Leo is free.

beats.scene: Leo types a message on his phone on a quiet Sunday evening
beats.summary: On Sunday night Leo texts Mira to ask if she can work an extra afternoon, and no answer comes.

beats.scene: Mira checks her phone as Leo watches her from across the shop
beats.summary: Mira arrives on Monday afternoon, quiet and pale, and checks her phone while Leo watches stiffly.

beats.scene: Leo mutters behind the counter, imagining what Mira must be thinking
beats.summary: Leo decides that Mira must be angry with him, and his mind builds a story to explain her silence.

beats.scene: Mira pulls on her coat and leaves early, the door closing softly
beats.summary: Leo answers in short, cold words all afternoon, and Mira leaves early without explaining.

beats.scene: Leo stares at his bedroom ceiling at night, thoughts swirling above him
beats.summary: At night Leo lies awake while his mind fills the empty space with stories, mostly the worst ones.

beats.scene: Ada listens over the garden wall with her head tilted like a bird
beats.summary: Ada hears the story and asks Leo what the facts are, and he finds that there is only one.

beats.scene: Ada stands on a ferry deck at sunrise beside a pale passenger
beats.summary: Ada tells how a pale passenger at the rail of the Gull seemed deeply upset, and he was only seasick.

beats.scene: Ada writes two short columns on a notepad: facts and stories
beats.summary: Ada helps Leo to separate what he knows from what he has imagined, and almost everything lands in the story column.

beats.scene: A half-finished jigsaw puzzle lies on a kitchen table
beats.summary: Ada says that the mind fills every gap like a jigsaw, but a guess is only a guess, however confident it feels.

beats.scene: Ada holds up the third card beside the small stack of the others
beats.summary: Ada gives Leo the third card: ask before you decide what is true.

beats.scene: Leo unlocks the shop door in grey morning light, hesitating
beats.summary: Leo opens the shop on Wednesday, still feeling the pull of his story, and decides to ask Mira directly.

beats.scene: Leo breathes slowly beside the workbench as Mira takes off her coat
beats.summary: When Mira arrives, Leo takes one breath and asks whether his message reached her.

beats.scene: Mira holds a phone with a badly cracked, blank screen
beats.summary: Mira explains that her phone fell from her bicycle on Sunday and went black, so she never saw the message.

beats.scene: Leo laughs and shakes his head with a hand on his forehead
beats.summary: Leo laughs at himself for spending two days angry about a broken phone.

beats.scene: Ada draws a question mark on a napkin beside an open hand
beats.summary: Ada says that a good question is simple, curious and open, and asks what happened more than why you did it.

beats.scene: Leo greets Mira at the shop door with a steady, curious look
beats.summary: Leo tries an open question on Mira when she is late: what happened this morning?

beats.scene: Leo listens with his phone face down on the counter
beats.summary: Leo puts his phone face down and listens to Mira's whole answer without interrupting, and learns more than he expected.

beats.scene: A customer talks fast beside a flat tyre while Leo listens and nods
beats.summary: A customer arrives complaining about a repair, and when Leo listens to the end she says all she needs is a quick adjustment.

beats.scene: Leo repeats a customer's request aloud while writing it down
beats.summary: Leo learns to say back what he has heard, so that both people know that they have understood each other.

beats.scene: Ada reads a notebook page headed Questions while sipping her tea
beats.summary: Leo shows Ada a new page of questions asked, and she says that the more he asks, the less he has to guess.

beats.scene: Leo sighs loudly in a crowded shop while Mira sweeps past
beats.summary: Saturdays are getting busy and Leo needs help, but he only hints at it, and Mira does not understand.

beats.scene: Leo writes a clear request on a note and hands it to Mira
beats.summary: Leo writes a clear note asking Mira to work Saturday mornings in March, and says what he needs and why.

beats.scene: Mira reads the note, smiling, with a pencil in her hand
beats.summary: Mira says yes to the Saturdays and asks for one Friday afternoon a month off, and they agree on a fair deal.

beats.scene: A deckhand struggles alone with a heavy rope at the ferry quay
beats.summary: Ada tells how a deckhand once strained his back because he never asked for help with a heavy rope.

beats.scene: Leo holds a pen over a delivery form while Pavel reads it
beats.summary: Leo asks Pavel to write down delivery days in advance, and for the first time he knows when parcels will arrive.

beats.scene: Leo compares two price lists, one on a laptop, one on paper
beats.summary: Leo compares the supplier's price on his laptop with the one in the paper catalogue and finds that they differ.

beats.scene: Leo phones the supplier with the paper catalogue open at the page
beats.summary: Leo telephones the supplier and learns that the paper catalogue is a year old, so the laptop price is the true one.

beats.scene: Leo on a train watches a frowning stranger and shrugs gently
beats.summary: On a train, Leo watches a frowning stranger and decides to treat his guess as a guess and not as a fact.

beats.scene: Leo greets a new customer with an open, friendly smile
beats.summary: Leo greets a harassed new customer with an open smile, taking the best view as a first guess to be tested.

beats.scene: A woman points down Harbour Road toward the café, laughing
beats.summary: The harassed stranger turns out to be lost, and she only wanted directions to Gus's cafe.

beats.scene: Bram whispers over his shop doorstep to Nell and a passing neighbour
beats.summary: Bram says that the council will close Harbour Road for a week, and the rumour spreads from shop to shop.

beats.scene: Leo speaks on the telephone with a notepad and a patient face
beats.summary: Leo telephones the council to ask, and learns that only the crossing near the bridge will close, for two days.

beats.scene: Leo tells Bram and Nell the council's real plans at the bakery door
beats.summary: Leo shares the real facts with his neighbours, and the worry along Harbour Road melts away.

beats.scene: Leo telephones his sister while a paper calendar hangs on the wall
beats.summary: Ines has not called for a week, and instead of guessing that she is hurt, Leo telephones and asks.

beats.scene: Ada pours tea and wags a finger gently over the wall
beats.summary: Ada warns that asking is not questioning someone to death: ask once, kindly, and then believe what you hear.

beats.scene: A customer shrugs warmly at the counter while Leo smiles back
beats.summary: Sometimes the answer to a question is I do not know, and Leo learns to say thank you for that too.

beats.scene: Leo juggles a ringing phone, a customer and a notebook at the counter
beats.summary: On a tricky busy day Leo uses all three rules at once: he checks before promising, breathes, and asks.

beats.scene: Mira leans on the counter, smiling, as Leo closes the till
beats.summary: Mira says that the shop feels different, and that Leo does too, and he says only that he is trying.

beats.scene: Ada adds the third card to a small stack under a smooth stone
beats.summary: Ada puts the third card on the stack under a smooth stone, saying rule three replaces worry and guessing with an honest question.

beats.scene: Ada holds the last white card face down against her chest
beats.summary: Ada keeps the last card face down and says that the fourth rule is different: it is about what Leo leaves behind.

beats.scene: Boxes and packing paper cover the shop floor after a huge delivery
beats.summary: A huge spring delivery leaves the shop floor strewn with boxes and packing paper, and Leo feels overwhelmed.

beats.scene: Leo sits on a stool in the middle of the boxes, doing nothing

B1B2: Leo runs a small bicycle shop on Harbour Road, and this week almost everything has gone wrong. He has said yes to everyone, and now he feels tired, hurried and tangled.
On Monday, a customer called Kemal wheeled in a bicycle with a bent wheel. Leo said it would be ready by Friday, although he had not even looked at his work list.
On Tuesday, Nell from the bakery next door asked for her delivery bike to be mended by Wednesday morning. Leo said yes at once, because saying no to a neighbour felt rude and a little frightening.
On Wednesday, Mira, who works three afternoons a week, pointed at the chart above the bench. Three different jobs were promised for the same hour, and not one of them was small.
That evening, Leo's friend Joss telephoned to ask for help carrying boxes on Saturday afternoon. Leo said, “Of course, no problem,” even though his work list was already far too long.
On Thursday, Leo waits all day for a parcel from Pavel, the parts driver. It never comes, because Leo forgot to confirm the order.
Friday arrives, and every yes that Leo has given seems to come due at once. He eats one dry biscuit standing up and answers the phone with his mouth full.
Kemal arrives at six o'clock, as promised, and finds his bicycle in the corner with its wheel still off. He says very little, which feels worse than an angry speech, and then he leaves.
When the door is locked, Leo sits on a crate and thinks about his week. Nell's bicycle was late, Joss is expecting him on Saturday, and Kemal went home without his bike.
Leo steps into the small back yard to get some cool air. Over the low garden wall, the light in his neighbour Ada's kitchen is warm, and somebody is humming.
Ada, wearing an old woollen hat, is watering her plants in the last of the light. She sees Leo's face, says nothing about it, and holds out a hot mug of tea over the wall.
Leo starts with Kemal's bicycle and ends up telling her everything. Ada does not interrupt once, and by the time he stops talking, his tea has gone cool.
Ada tells him that she was the captain of the ferry called the Gull for forty years. Every day she carried people, bicycles and sometimes a goat across the grey bay.
Ada says that nobody can steer a ferry in a storm with a hundred clever ideas. What helped her was a handful of clear rules that she never had to argue about.
Leo follows Ada into her warm kitchen, where a paper checklist hangs beside the window. Pilots and sailors use lists like this one, she says, and she has never stopped using hers.
When we are tired, Ada says, the mind forgets even the things it knows very well. A short list does the remembering, so that the mind is free to think.
Ada tells him that he is not careless, because careless people do not feel ashamed. His real trouble is that he has no rules for the moments when he is tired.
Ada opens a kitchen drawer and takes out four plain white cards and a pen. She says that she will write four rules for Leo, and that she will write them only once.
Ada writes with great care, stopping after each word to think about it. She says that a rule with a careless word in it is like a rope with a weak strand.

Ada reads the four rules aloud: mean what you say, pause before you answer, ask before you decide, and leave things better. She will give him the cards one at a time, she says, because a rule only helps once it has become a habit.
On Saturday morning, Kemal comes back to the shop. Leo does not make excuses; he says that he is sorry and that he should never have promised Friday.
Kemal explains that he starts work at five at the fish market, when no buses run. He had arranged his whole week around a bicycle that Leo promised for Friday.
Pavel's van arrives at ten with the right wheel, and Leo fits it in forty minutes. The job itself was small; the trouble was a promise made without thinking.
Kemal pays, wheels his bike to the door, and turns around. “Next time,” he says, “tell me the day it can really be done, not the day I want to hear.”
At noon, Nell comes for her delivery bicycle, which is three days late. She tells him, with a small smile, that she has been delivering bread from a pram.
Leo arrives at Joss's new flat at four, long after the work began. The boxes are already inside, and Joss has carried most of them alone.
Walking home along the harbour, Leo adds it all up. Three people were let down, he is exhausted, and his easy yeses have bought him nothing at all.
On Sunday morning, Leo buys a bag of warm buns from Nell and knocks on Ada's door. He wants to tell her that he is ready to hear the first rule.
Ada listens to the story of Saturday and then pours the tea. She says that Leo has already done the hardest part, which is noticing what his words have cost.
Ada takes the first white card from her pocket and puts it in front of him. In plain upright letters it says: Mean what you say.
Ada explains that many sentences are small promises, such as I'll call you or see you soon. She asks Leo to do nothing but count his promises for one day.
On Monday, Leo counts his promises on his fingers: a call, an email, a visit, a coffee. By lunchtime he has made seven, and he has hardly noticed any of them.
Leo writes down the phrases that hide promises: leave it with me, I'll look into it, and no problem. Each one sounds friendly, but each one makes someone wait.
Mira laughs when he tells her what he is doing. In July, she says, he promised her a new stool, and she is still sitting on the wobbly one.
That evening Leo writes down every promise he has not yet kept. He marks the ones he can really do, and he plans to tell the others the truth.
Ada tells him that a short list you keep is worth more than a long list you forget. Before he says yes, he should look honestly at the work in front of him.
A customer asks for a quick repair, and Leo's mouth almost says yes. Instead he says that he will check his stock and telephone by four o'clock.
Leo counts his spare tubes and reads his work list before he gives anyone a date. The real answer, he finds, is Wednesday, which is much better than a false Monday.
At four o'clock exactly, Leo telephones the customer with his honest answer. She is so surprised that she laughs and says, “Nobody ever calls back when they say they will.”
Leo tells Ada over the wall that keeping one small promise felt surprisingly good. She says that this is how trust begins, with one kept word and then another.
A few days later, Nell's bicycle chain snaps, and she asks Leo to mend it before six tomorrow morning. He feels the old yes rising, but he looks at his work list instead.
Leo tells her honestly that six o'clock is not possible. He offers to bring the bicycle to her door by noon instead, and Nell nods and says that is fair.
Bram from the hardware shop asks Leo to service three family bicycles by tomorrow. Leo smiles, shakes his head, and offers to do one now and two next week.
Ada tells Leo that a kind no usually has three small parts. Thank the person, be clear about what you cannot do, and offer what you really can.
Leo's sister Ines telephones and asks him to run her market stall on Sunday. He says no, kindly and clearly, and offers to lend her his folding table instead.
Mira asks if she can leave an hour early on Friday. Leo checks the work list, sees that he can manage, and says yes and means it.
Leo had always believed that saying no would make people dislike him. In three weeks nobody has done so, and several people seem to trust him more.
A customer asks Leo to leave the worn brakes alone to save money. Leo says no, because that would not be safe, and he shows her exactly why.
Two days later, the customer returns with a smile. She says that the new brakes feel like a different bicycle, and she thanks Leo for not taking the easy way.
Leo notices that his evenings have become much quieter than they used to be. Fewer promises mean fewer worries, and he tells Ada that he slept well for the first time in months.
After dropping a box of spokes, Leo sees his tired face in the shop window. “You are useless,” he mutters, and he hardly notices that he has said it.
Ada steps inside and asks him one simple question. Would he ever say those words to a friend, or to a customer who had dropped something?
For one day, Leo listens to the words he says to himself. He hears stupid, hopeless and typical before lunch, and he is shocked by how often they come.
Ada writes two sentences on a scrap of card: I made a mistake, and I am a mistake. The first is honest and useful, she says, and the second is simply untrue.
Leo ruins the first wheel he tries to straighten, and the old words rise in his mouth. He says instead, “That one went wrong, so I'll do it again,” and the second try is easy.
Bram and Nell are whispering by the fence about Gus, who runs the café. Leo knows that one small joke would make him feel part of the group.
Bram turns and asks Leo what he thinks about Gus and the café that keeps closing. Leo says honestly, “I don't know, but you could ask him,” and goes back to work.
Ada tells Leo that on the Gull, a rumour once spread about a young deckhand. It was false, but it took months for people to trust him again.
When Bram asks who built such a straight wheel, Leo says that it was Mira, the best wheel builder he has met. Mira is not in the room, and he means every word.
Later, Leo tells Mira to her face that her wheels are the best he has seen. She blushes, and then she works with her head held a little higher.
Leo buys a small blue notebook and writes the word Promises across the top of the first page. Every time he gives his word, he will write it down at once.
On Tuesday afternoon, Leo finishes a repair that he had promised for four o'clock. He puts a neat tick in the notebook, and he is surprised by how good it feels.
By the end of the week, Leo has made six promises, and he has kept all six. The page of ticks looks small, but he feels lighter than he has in years.
Leo has promised Sam a new pair of wheels for his daughter's birthday on Saturday. On Wednesday, a storm closes the coast road, and Pavel's van cannot get through.
Leo could wait and hope, but he knows that would be unfair to Sam. Instead he decides to ring on Thursday morning, as soon as he knows the truth.
Leo tells Sam plainly that the wheels will not arrive by Saturday, and that he is truly sorry. He offers a loan bicycle for the birthday, free of charge.
Sam is disappointed, but he thanks Leo for calling so early. Because he knows now, he has time to plan a better surprise for his daughter.
On Saturday, Sam's daughter rides the loan bicycle with a ribbon on the handlebar. On Monday the road reopens, and Leo carries her new wheels to her door himself.
Kemal drops in and sees the notebook on the counter. He has heard how Leo called Sam early, he says, and in a small town a kept word travels fast.
Ada places the first card face up in the middle of her kitchen table. Rule one, she says, does not make a person trusted overnight; it builds trust one kept promise at a time.
